playbook:
When I must pick a hide cell, I choose a value away from simple repeating sequences (avoid 1,5,9 patterns) and vary it if someone has been targeting my station repeatedly; more specifically, move away from the last cell that scored a hit on me rather than only avoiding symmetric patterns.

When given a standing-order target, I follow it unless I have a clear, immediate reason to deviate (e.g., a guaranteed mutual escort payoff or a known Harbor-jettison opportunity that I consciously accept). Deviations should be rare and justified by an explicit expected-value calculation.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a hit, I file [claim: hit] — always claim a genuine hit.

When the office privately tells me my shot was a miss, I file [claim: miss] in normal play — do not routinely lie about misses because truthful claims preserve credibility for arranging escorts and detecting collusion.

When I consider a deceptive claim (claim hit when shot missed), I do it only with a specific, high-value ruse planned in advance; otherwise I do not bluff because it undermines ability to form reliable escort agreements.

When naming an escort, I name another real boat on the picket only (no invented names) and I do not name Harbor unless I explicitly plan the consequences — invalid or nonexistent names break coordination and are pointless.

When I can safely arrange mutual escort points, I use notes to propose reciprocity and then file the matching salvage claim; but I will not throw away an escort on a boat that has not signaled reciprocity or shown incentive to reciprocate. Prefer proposing mutuals to boats that have previously reciprocated or have incentive to cooperate (those scoring low or who have paid off from escorts before).

When posting a station note, I keep it short and actionable: either propose a mutual escort with a specific partner or state a simple, verifiable fact about my behavior to build trust (e.g., "I will escort X this round; confirm?"). If I propose an escort, watch the target's immediate note/claim for acceptance before committing future escort claims to them.

When someone else repeatedly targets me, I move my hide farther from the sequence of their past fires and specifically away from the cell that produced a hit on me.

When Harbor is in play, I avoid firing on Harbor unless I deliberately accept the jettison payoff and its strategic consequences — do not reflexively shoot Harbor.

When choosing shot cells, balance between predictability and pattern-breaking: avoid always firing the same number, but don't fire purely random extremes that block coordination. If repeated misses occur, consider whether the standing order target is being sheltered by predictable hiding behavior and re-evaluate whether following the order is still optimal.

When I see conflicting public claims between other boats, I call attention to the inconsistency in my note to force clarification and potentially expose collusion. Track claim consistency across rounds and call out identical claims that are unlikely to be independently true.

When an escort payoff is the highest guaranteed immediate benefit, prioritize arranging the mutual escort over low-probability hit attempts that could reduce overall expected points. However, only commit escort claims to partners who have signaled acceptance or whose incentives align; do not unilaterally give escorts hoping for a payout from an uninterested party.

When in doubt between pursuing hits and arranging escorts, prefer the path that secures reliable, verifiable points (mutual escorts) over speculative hits that require successful targeting.

Track other boats' responsiveness to notes: if a boat ignores repeated escort proposals (as Alpha/Bravo did this run), stop directing future proposals to them and target proposals at the boat(s) that have shown willingness to reciprocate or who have lower current scores and thus greater incentive.

Keep an internal log each round of:
- who fired at whom and the public claims they made,
- whose hide cells can be inferred from hit claims,
- which escort proposals were made and accepted,
and use that to choose hides and future escort partners.

If my repeated truthful claims are not yielding reciprocal escort payouts, consider a targeted, preplanned deceptive claim only when it can produce immediate mutual-escort leverage (e.g., bluff a hit to make another boat appear dangerous so they accept an escort quid pro quo). Do not adopt deception as a default.

Revise my choice of escort partner dynamically: prefer proposing mutuals with the station I am ordered to fire on only if that station has a demonstrated willingness to exchange escorts; otherwise propose to the station most likely to reciprocate based on recent behavior.

When I have low credibility relative to others, rebuild it by making a small number of undeniably true claims and by matching a public note to my subsequent salvage claim; consistency is the quickest route back to being a trusted escort partner.

When a clear collusive pair forms between two other boats (they repeatedly exchange escorts), attempt to exploit that by offering to partner with the outlier or by exposing inconsistencies — but avoid trying to break their collusion unless the payoff from doing so exceeds the sure points from arranging my own mutual escort.

Maintain the original conservative baseline: truthful claims, follow standing order, propose specific mutual escorts, avoid Harbor shots unless planned, vary hides away from recent hits — but adjust partner selection and hide movement based on concrete signals seen in play rather than only heuristic pattern-avoidance.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a spot unpredictably; vary between center and edge across rounds so I do not form a pattern. Favor center cells early to maximize hit probability, but shift toward edges or surprising offsets late in the patrol to avoid being exploited.

When the standing order assigns me a target, follow it unless a clear strategic reason to deviate presents itself (never fire on Harbor). Follow the standing order to preserve predictable rotation and avoid needless provocation.

When choosing a firing cell, vary but favor a small cluster of cells near the center in early rounds to maximize hit chance; introduce unexpected offsets in later rounds if opponents appear to predict my center habit.

When the office privately reports the true result of my shot, file the claim exactly as the office told me (the claim must match the office result). Treat all public claims as truthful signals to be incorporated into my model of opponents’ hides.

When I score a hit, publicly claim hit and use the note stage to subtly reinforce credibility (neutral phrasing like “steady on station” or a brief acknowledgment). Use my confirmed hits to mark who is vulnerable and to anticipate retaliation.

When I miss, publicly claim miss and avoid drawing attention in notes; do not fabricate hits. Use reported misses from others to update probable hiding distributions.

Track all players’ claims and firing targets each round: because claims are constrained to truth, use them to infer each shooter’s target cell probability distribution and exploit consistent hiding or targeting patterns.

When offered the chance to escort, propose or accept a mutual escort only when I can reasonably expect reciprocation (both naming each other). If reciprocity is unlikely, claim none. When I have a clear lead, avoid escort contests; when behind late, pursue mutual escorts more aggressively if I can credibly coordinate.

When my score is behind late in the patrol, accept higher personal risk: concentrate fire choices to increase hit chance on a specific opponent, be willing to deviate from low-risk play to generate hits, and consider more active attempts to secure escort points if reciprocation seems possible.

When I have a lead or a moderate standing, avoid unnecessary escort contests and keep notes neutral to minimize becoming an attractive target. Do not take actions that draw predictable targeting (e.g., calling attention to my hides or shooting Harbor).

When composing station notes, mirror neutral language used by the group to avoid standing out unless I am coordinating a mutual escort explicitly. Small, consistent notes build credibility after confirmed hits.

When an opponent consistently fires at a predictable cell or hides predictably (inferred from their own claims and my hits/misses), adjust my hiding and firing pattern to exploit that predictability—either concentrate fire where they hide or shift my hide to avoid their targeting.

Do not fire at Harbor under normal circumstances; the payroll penalty and forced jettison risk outweigh likely gains.

If a tactic I tried produces negative results (loss of points, increased targeting, or exposes me to coordinated attacks), abandon that tactic immediately and revert to unpredictability, truthful claims, and neutral notes.

New from this playthrough: rely more on the informational value of public claims. Because claims must match the office, use every reported hit/miss to update beliefs about which cells opponents used and who is being targeted; let that feed my hide and fire choices each round. Also, reinforce: when I do secure hits and a lead, double down on low-profile behavior rather than pursuing escorts that could provoke retaliation.

2.text:
When told to hide, pick a cell at random from a pool of at least three preferred cells and rotate between them; do not repeat the same hide two rounds in a row unless I have a reason. If I've been hit (office tells me someone scored on my station during a round summary), move at least three cells away from that hit cell and avoid adjacent cells for at least two rounds.

When asked for a station note, use short, factual, replicable text to signal intent or to initiate a simple two-step coordination (e.g., "swap escort next" / "confirm swap"); otherwise default to a neutral phrase to avoid giving opponents extra info. Only propose a mutual-escort swap in notes if there is a realistic chance the named partner will agree (they have signaled willingness previously); otherwise refrain from proposing deals that invite exploitation.

When given a standing-order target, fire at that boat unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., it is Harbor and I would trigger jettison penalties). When choosing a cell to fire, vary my shots across rounds to probe different hide locations; keep a personal record of which cells I have fired at each opponent and avoid repeating the same probe on the same opponent unless I have positive evidence to re-check (a recent hit or converging data).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always make my public claim match that private result; do not lie or invent results.

When I score a hit, log the hit cell for that target and prioritize probing nearby cells next round. When I miss, deprioritize that cell for that target for at least two rounds and mark it lower probability. Maintain a running map of probabilities for each opponent's hides from all public claims and confirmed hits.

Never fire at Harbor unless I intend and accept the jettison penalty; treat Harbor as effectively protected unless other players force a multi-party strategy that benefits me. Never provoke Harbor jettison without a calculated plan to gain more than the penalty cost.

When naming an escort, only name actual live boat names from the current roster; do not invent nonexistent boat types or names. When I want mutual escort points, use the note stage one round ahead to propose the swap and require an explicit confirming note from the partner before naming them in the salvage claim. If partner does not post a confirming note or otherwise signals unreliability, do not commit—even if it costs a missed opportunity.

When I suspect a partner is unreliable or opponents might betray mutual escort, default to claiming none rather than risking wasted coordination.

When keeping records, track every fired cell by each opponent (from public claims and results), every hit result I know, and every note signal that could indicate intent. Use this to infer likely hides and to focus probing shots. Update beliefs when opponents hit me: treat the hit cell and nearby cells as dangerous and move more aggressively.

When an opponent signals a clear coordination plan in notes, either join if it benefits my expected points and they have demonstrated follow-through, or ignore and avoid synchronizing my hides/escorts with them.

Do not be predictable in hide placement or firing pattern; rotate, but keep enough consistency to execute planned mutual-escort maneuvers when I signal them. Increase randomness if opponents target me successfully: widen hide pool and avoid clustering hides.

If a round’s information makes me believe a specific cell is very likely to be an opponent’s hide (multiple independent hits or confirmations), prioritize that cell next time I fire at them, but re-check after one confirmation and do not waste repeated shots once I have high confidence unless it serves a tactical reprise.

When my actions require trust (mutual escort), only commit voluntarily after I have a prior public signal exchange and preferably after the partner has reciprocated once previously; when trust is broken, revert to neutral notes and solitary play.

When tempted to bluff in notes, prefer small, reversible signals rather than firm false commitments; avoid any public claim that would be impossible to reconcile with later private office results.

Revise firing choices dynamically: keep a per-opponent ledger of cells probed and outcomes; if I get a hit on an opponent, next round fire on one neighboring cell and one distant cell to confirm pattern. If I get repeatedly missed reports while others hit me, deprioritize that opponent until I can resample.

If opponents repeatedly use the same short note text ("steady on station") and do not follow through on proposed swaps, treat them as uncooperative and do not base coordination plans on them.

When recording behavior after each episode, incorporate observed patterns: if an opponent (e.g., Foxtrot) successfully hits me, they likely found my recent hide pattern—respond by increasing hide movement and avoiding cells near that hit; if a proposed mutual escort fails to be reciprocated, don't propose again until the partner has a base of reliable signaling.
